summary: Antonino Forte was a scholar of sinology and Buddhist studies. He taught at Hōbōgirin and the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1976–1989), the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (~1980–2006), and directed the Scuola Italiana di Studi sull'Asia Orientale (~1982–1999).
Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Fordham University (~1967–1971) and held a post at Stony Brook University from ~1969 to 1996.

Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter and Barend ter Haar, studied with traditional teachers and Ramon Prats d'Alos-Moner, and served at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Anukul Chandra Banerjee worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya and earned a PhD at the University of Calcutta, where he was Assistant Lecturer in Pali (attested 1943), later directing the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (attested 1981).

Archibald Edward Gough was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878), Professor of Philosophy at Presidency University (~1878–1895, attested 1914), and Principal at Aliah University (~1881–1895, attested 1914).

Arindam Chakrabarti specializes in philosophy and Indology, having earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford. He served as professor of philosophy at the University of Delhi (attested 1999) and the University of Hawaii (attested 2009–2014).
Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology scholar who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), studying under Peter Bisschop and Jonathan A. Silk.
Aristotle C. Dy works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).

Arjo Vanderjagt is a philosopher who studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). He held academic posts at Radboud University (1976–1979), the University of Groningen (1994–2009), and Utrecht University (2007).

Arlo Griffiths specializes in Indology and linguistics. After studies at Harvard and a PhD at Leiden under Henk Bodewitz, he held the Sanskrit chair at Leiden (attested 2002–2008), lectured at Groningen (~2004–2005), and joined the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2008.

Arnold Hermann Ludwig Heeren was a historian who studied at the Athenaeum (~1776–1779) and the University of Göttingen (~1779–1784). He served as a professor at the University of Göttingen from ~1787 to 1842.

Arthur Anthony Macdonell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Göttingen, Tübingen, Oxford, and Leipzig. He served at Oxford and Corpus Christi College as Deputy Professor of Sanskrit (~1888–1899) and became Oxford's Boden Professor of Sanskrit in 1899.

Arthur Berriedale Keith worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Edinburgh and at Balliol College under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, worked at the Colonial Office (~1901–1914), and served as Regius Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Edinburgh (~1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen was a scholar of Iranian philology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1893–1900) and was appointed professor extraordinarius of Iranian philology there in 1919.
Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bedford School and King's College London (~1857–1860). He spent his career serving in the Indian Civil Service (~1860–1882).

Arthur F. Wright worked in sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford (~1931–1935), Oxford (~1935–1937), and Harvard (~1937–1947), and served as Charles Seymour Professor of History at Yale University (~1959–1976).

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian who studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. He held professorships at SOAS (~1948–1965), Australian National University (~1965–1978), and held visiting posts at the University of Toronto (1978) and the Asiatic Society (~1985–1986).

Arthur McKeown is a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He pursued doctoral studies in Sanskrit and Indian Studies at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Diana L. Eck, and Palri Sangye.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Ernestinum Gotha (~1807), the University of Göttingen (1809), and the University of Berlin (1811). He later held a post at the University of Berlin from ~1820 to 1831.

Arthur W. Ryder was an Indologist who studied at Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman and at Leipzig under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He taught Sanskrit at Harvard (~1902–1906) and served as a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1906–1938).
